page.layout: One column of running text, page 659. Below the text, at the foot left, the gathering signature "Tt 2" with the end of the last line running beside it. No margin notes and no running head.

main_text.p: quod satis sit pro afferente, atque teste. Quod salus hominum per homines est, cui posthac nihil addendum esse contendas.

Videatur etiam [illegible, ~12 letters] Ioannes Teiunator, [illegible, ~10 letters] Theodorus Abbas Monasterij [illegible, ~6 letters] Alastadiun, qui difertissime, & fusissime de hac scripserunt materia, vt nec ipsas minutissimas ad illam spectantes prætermiserint circumstantias. Nunc ad celeberrimam de Purgatorio quaestionem.

De Purgatorio fuse egimus in notis ad Catalogum librorum Hebediesu pagina 165. & seqq. vbi diximus primo loco, Orientales, Syros præsertim, nomine [illegible, ~5 letters] Sciul, seu Inferni intelligere tam locum, in quo cruciantur Damnati æternum, quam eum, in quo animæ leuioribus criminibus, & maculis coinquinatæ purgantur, atque (licet nomine differat) re tamen ipsa eundem esse, ac Romanum Purgatorium. Quinimo nunc addimus ibi dictis, nomine [illegible, ~5 letters] Scial apud Chaldæos de solo loco, in quo animæ ad tempus cruciantur, intelligi. Quod quidem con-stat

page.notes: The Arabic-script lines (the two lines of names and the Syriac/Arabic forms of Sciul and Scial) are not legible to me letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The Latin names beside them are transcribed as printed. The first Latin word "quod" in the first paragraph is italic. The page is continued from the previous page, hence cont="true". The word "stat" on the last line completes "con-" and stands beside the signature; I have joined it. The text is printed as "vbi", "vt" and "fusi-" with the original spelling retained, except for u/v and long s which are normalised as required.
